items.title: ticket (tk)
items.text: Minimal, offline task tracker with DAG dependency intelligence. Built with for both human developers and autonomous AI coding agents.

items.title: 💡 Key Highlights
items.text:
• Zero Database / Pure Plain Text: State resides in .tickets/*.md files with YAML frontmatter, versioned by Git.
  • DAG Dependency Tracking: Native support for parent-child hierarchies, blockers, cycle detection, and automated downstream unblocking.
  • Unix Speed: Core CLI runs on portable POSIX Bash with zero mandatory runtime dependencies (no Python or Node required for base CLI).
  • Built for AI Agents First: Deterministic 5-step agent execution loop, built-in agent skill (agent-skill/tk/SKILL.md), and machine-readable llms.txt endpoints.

items.title: ⚡ Quick Installation
items.text:
Install the zero-dependency Bash CLI or the full suite with the interactive Web UI:

git clone https://github.com/msampathkumar/ticket.git
cd ticket

# Full Suite (CLI + Web UI + Agent Skill) — default
./install.sh --full

# Core CLI Only (Pure Bash, zero Python dependencies)
./install.sh --core

items.title: 🤖 Install Agent Skill via NPX
items.text:
Equip your AI coding assistant with the tk skill in a single command without cloning:

npx github:msampathkumar/ticket agent-skill --install

items.title: 🧭 Machine-Readable Agent Docs (llms.txt)
items.text: As part of our commitment to being super agent-friendly: - /llms.txt: Structured table of contents linking directly to all markdown documentation files. - /llms-full.txt: Consolidated single-file documentation reference combining all specifications into one payload.

items.title: tk - AI Agent Guidelines & Integration Guide
items.text: This document outlines best practices and rules for AI coding assistants and autonomous agents (e.g. Antigravity, Claude, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI) when operating within repositories tracked by tk.

items.title: 1. Why tk is Ideal for AI Agents
items.text:
• File-Centric State: AI agents can read and write tickets using standard file and CLI tools without managing database connections.
  • Topological Dependency Order: tk ready prevents agents from picking up blocked tasks out of order.
  • Audit Trails in Markdown: Agents can record reasoning, test results, and review comments directly in the ticket file.

items.title: 2. Standard Workflow for AI Agents
items.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Agent scans ready tasks via `tk ready`] --> B[Select next actionable ticket]
    B --> C[Mark in-progress via `tk start <id>`]
    C --> D[Implement & verify code changes]
    D --> E[Append review notes via `tk add-note <id> "..."]
    E --> F[Close ticket via `tk close <id>`]

items.title: Step 1: Discover Actionable Work
items.text:
Run tk ready to list open tickets whose dependencies are already resolved: 

tk ready

items.title: Step 2: Mark Task in Progress
items.text:
Inform human developers and other agents that the ticket is being worked on: 

tk start <ticket-id>

items.title: Step 3: Check Subtasks and Design Requirements
items.text:
View ticket specifications, design notes, and acceptance checklist: 

tk show <ticket-id>

items.title: Step 4: Record Progress & Notes
items.text:
Append timestamped notes detailing the verification results or implementation choices: 

tk add-note <ticket-id> "Implemented visual tree with horizontal orientation and verified locally."

items.title: Step 5: Mark Complete
items.text:
Close the ticket after test execution: 

tk close <ticket-id>

items.title: 3. Subtask Decomposition Pattern
items.text:
When an agent encounters a large epic or complex feature: 1. Create subtasks with --parent <epic-id>: 

tk create "Implement backend API endpoint" --parent <epic-id> -t task
tk create "Build frontend UI modal" --parent <epic-id> -t task
2. Wire dependencies between subtasks: 
tk dep <frontend-id> <backend-id>

items.title: 4. Agent Skill Installation
items.text:
Agents supporting custom skills can install the tk skill definition directly into ~/.agents/skills/tk/SKILL.md: 

./install.sh --skill

items.title: tk - Plugin Architecture & Development Guide
items.text: tk features an extensible, lightweight plugin system that allows extending functionality without modifying the core CLI script.

items.title: 1. How Plugins Work
items.text:
When you execute: 

tk <command> [args...]
The tk dispatcher first checks for an executable named tk-<command> or ticket-<command> in your system $PATH. If found, tk delegates execution directly to that plugin binary or script.

To bypass plugins and run a built-in command directly, use tk super <command>.

items.title: 2. Environment Context Passed to Plugins
items.text:
When tk launches a plugin, it automatically exports two environment variables:

  • TICKETS_DIR: The absolute path to the active .tickets directory.
  • TK_SCRIPT: The absolute path to the root tk executable.

Plugins can call built-in commands by executing: 

"$TK_SCRIPT" super <command> [args...]

items.title: 3.1 Help Discovery Metadata
items.text:
To enable tk help to automatically list and describe your plugin:

Shell / Python Scripts: Include a comment in the first 10 lines: 

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tk-plugin: Interactive Kanban Web UI & PR review dashboard
# tk-plugin-version: 0.2.0

Compiled Binaries: Implement the --tk-describe flag: 

$ my-plugin --tk-describe
tk-plugin: Interactive Kanban Web UI & PR review dashboard

items.title: 3.2 Version Flag
items.text:
All plugins should implement --version or -v flag to output their version: 

$ tk-webui --version
tk-webui 0.2.0

items.title: 4. Modularity & Optional Installation
items.text:
Plugins must be strictly optional. Users who only need the zero-dependency Bash CLI should never be required to install Python, Node.js, or external runtimes. The core tk script has no hard-coded knowledge of any plugin: whatever is installed in $PATH is auto-discovered and listed by tk help with its one-line # tk-plugin: description.

install.sh exposes one target per component; flags accumulate, so any combination works (e.g. ./install.sh --core --github): - --core: Installs only tk CLI. - --webui: Installs only the Web UI plugin. - --skill: Installs the agent skill. - --github: Installs the optional GitHub sync plugin (tk-github). - --scion-taskforce: Installs the optional SCION Task Force orchestrator (tk-scion-taskforce). - --full (default): Installs CLI, Web UI, and Agent Skill. Optional plugins are not included; the installer prints how to add them. - --all: Installs everything, including optional plugins. - --help: Lists all targets.

A plugin may additionally ship its own install.sh (with --uninstall) inside plugins/<name>/. When it does, the top-level install.sh target must delegate to it so install logic lives in exactly one place (see plugins/scion-taskforce/install.sh).

items.title: 5. Official Plugins
items.text:
• tk webui (tk-webui): Full-featured interactive Kanban, Table, DAG Mind Map, and Timeline review dashboard.
  • tk github (tk-github): Syncs GitHub issues and PRs with local tickets, updates statuses on close/merge, and supports clean unsyncing. (optional)
  • tk scion-taskforce (tk-scion-taskforce): Single global daemon that launches a SCION coding worker for each ticket explicitly tagged taskforce, verifies the worker actually started, pauses it on waiting-for-review, and emits OpenTelemetry to local rotating logs. (optional; requires Python 3.9+ and the scion CLI)

items.title: 6. Example Plugin: tk-stats
items.text:
Here is a minimal plugin example (~/.local/bin/tk-stats):

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tk-plugin: Quick summary of open and closed ticket statistics
# tk-plugin-version: 1.0.0
set -euo pipefail

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--version" || "${1:-}" == "-v" ]]; then
    echo "tk-stats 1.0.0"
    exit 0
fi

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--tk-describe" ]]; then
    echo "tk-plugin: Quick summary of open and closed ticket statistics"
    exit 0
fi

TICKETS_DIR="${TICKETS_DIR:-.tickets}"

total=$(ls -1 "$TICKETS_DIR"/*.md 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo 0)
open=$("$TK_SCRIPT" super ready | wc -l || echo 0)
blocked=$("$TK_SCRIPT" super blocked | wc -l || echo 0)

echo "📊 Total Tickets : $total"
echo "🟢 Ready (Open)  : $open"
echo "🔴 Blocked       : $blocked"
Make it executable: 
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/tk-stats
tk stats

items.title: tk - Plugin Specification Standard (PLUGIN_SPEC.md)
items.text: Architecture and compliance requirements for tk plugins.

items.title: 1. Core Principles
items.text:
1. Decoupled: Plugins extend tk without modifying the core ticket CLI.
  2. Optional: Plugins are optional. Users who need only the core CLI never need external runtimes.
  3. Spec-Driven: Every plugin maintains a <PLUGIN-NAME>-SPEC.md specifying commands, flags, schema, and dependencies.
  4. Isolated: Each plugin lives in its own directory under plugins/<plugin-name>/.

items.title: 2. Directory Layout Standard
items.text:
Each plugin in the repository is organized in its own isolated subfolder:

plugins/
├── README.md
├── github/
│   ├── GITHUB-SPEC.md           # Plugin-specific specification
│   ├── ticket-github            # Executable binary / script
│   └── tk-github -> ticket-github
├── scion-taskforce/             # Python-backed plugin (thin bash entrypoint)
│   ├── SCION-TASKFORCE-SPEC.md
│   ├── install.sh               # Optional: standalone installer (--uninstall supported)
│   ├── scion-taskforce.yaml     # Optional: default config shipped with the plugin
│   ├── ticket-scion-taskforce   # Executable entrypoint
│   ├── tk-scion-taskforce -> ticket-scion-taskforce
│   └── tk_scion_taskforce/      # Plugin's own package; never imported by core
└── webui/
    └── WEBUI-SPEC.md -> ../../tk_webui/WEBUI-SPEC.md

items.title: 2.1 Installation Contract
items.text:
• The repo-level install.sh MUST offer a dedicated target per plugin (--<plugin-name>) and MUST NOT include optional plugins in the default --full bundle; only --all does.
  • A plugin MAY ship its own plugins/<name>/install.sh (supporting --uninstall). If it does, the repo-level target MUST delegate to it rather than duplicating the logic.
  • Installation MUST NOT touch the core ticket script. Discovery is purely by $PATH: once tk-<name> is installed, tk help lists it automatically using its # tk-plugin: description.

items.title: 3. Metadata & Discovery Contract
items.text: tk automatically discovers plugins available in $PATH matching tk-<command> or ticket-<command>.

items.title: 3.1 Header Comments (Scripts)
items.text:
Shell, Python, or Ruby scripts MUST include metadata comments in their first 10 lines: 

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tk-plugin: Single-line description of the plugin
# tk-plugin-version: 1.0.0

items.title: 3.2 Flags (Compiled Binaries)
items.text: Compiled binaries (Go, Rust, C) MUST implement: - --tk-describe: Prints tk-plugin: <description> to stdout and exits with code 0. - --version / -v: Prints <plugin-name> <version> to stdout and exits with code 0. - --help / -h: Displays standard usage and command help.

items.title: 4. Execution Protocol & Context
items.text: When tk <plugin-command> [args...] is executed: 1. tk resolves the target .tickets/ folder. 2. tk sets and exports environment variables: - TICKETS_DIR: Absolute path to .tickets/ directory. - TK_SCRIPT: Absolute path to tk executable. 3. tk invokes tk-<plugin-command> "$@" using exec.

items.title: 4.1 Calling Core Built-Ins
items.text:
Plugins can execute core tk routines without triggering recursion by using: 

"$TK_SCRIPT" super <built-in-command> [args...]

items.title: 5. Plugin Specification Template (<PLUGIN-NAME>-SPEC.md)
items.text: Each plugin's <PLUGIN-NAME>-SPEC.md must include: 1. Overview & Purpose: What the plugin does and why it exists. 2. Commands & CLI Flags: Exhaustive list of arguments and flags. 3. Data Schema / Metadata: Any tags, frontmatter keys, or file structures used. 4. Dependencies: External CLIs or runtimes required (e.g. gh, jq, python3). 5. Installation & Uninstallation: Instructions for installing and cleanly removing the plugin.

items.title: tk - System & Data Specification
items.text: Specification Lifecycle Architecture changes, format updates, and new features follow a spec-driven development lifecycle.

items.title: 1. System Goals & Philosophy
items.text: tk is a minimal, offline task tracker with dependency intelligence designed for developers and autonomous AI coding agents.

items.title: Core Principles
items.text:
1. Zero Database: State is stored locally in .tickets/*.md.
  2. Plain-Text Transparency: Every ticket is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter.
  3. DAG-Driven: Native dependency tracking (deps) enables topological sorting, cycle detection, and ready-queue computation.
  4. Unix Portability: Core CLI runs on POSIX Bash with awk and sed—no external runtime required.
  5. Decoupled Extensions: Web UI and external integrations operate as modular plugins.

items.title: 2.1 File Storage & Naming
items.text:
• Directory: .tickets/ (located in the repository root or discovered upwards in parent directories).
  • File Naming: <prefix>-<hash>.md (e.g., tic-6mex.md, msa-y8zi.md).
  • Prefix defaults to 3 characters derived from the folder name or random alphanumeric.
  • Hash is a 4-character random alphanumeric string ensuring local uniqueness.

items.title: 2.2 YAML Frontmatter Schema
items.text:
Each ticket file begins with a YAML header delimited by ---:

---
id: string          # Unique ticket identifier, e.g. tic-6mex (Required)
status: enum        # open | in_progress | closed (Required)
deps: list[string]  # Array of ticket IDs this ticket depends on (Required)
links: list[string] # Array of related ticket IDs (symmetric) (Optional)
created: ISO-8601   # Timestamp of ticket creation (e.g. 2026-09-25T10:01:06Z) (Required)
type: enum          # bug | feature | task | epic | chore (Default: task)
priority: integer   # 0 (Critical) to 4 (Trivial) (Default: 2)
assignee: string    # Assignee name or git username (Optional)
tags: list[string]  # Array of tag strings (Optional)
parent: string      # Parent ticket ID if this ticket is a subtask (Optional)
external_ref: string# External issue/PR reference, e.g. gh-123 (Optional)
---

items.title: 2.3 Markdown Body Structure
items.text:
Following the frontmatter, the Markdown body contains:

# <Title>

<Description text...>

## Design Notes
<Architecture or design thoughts...>

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2

## Review Notes / Audit Trail
<!-- Timestamped review comments appended by tk add-note -->
### Note (2026-09-25T10:30:00Z)
<Comment content>

items.title: 3.1 Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) Rules
items.text:
• A dependency A -> B (deps: [B]) means Ticket A is blocked by Ticket B.
  • Ticket A cannot be resolved or considered "Ready" until Ticket B is in closed status.
  • Symmetric links (links: [B]) denote relational associations without blocking semantics.

items.title: 3.2 State Queries
items.text:
• Ready Queue: All non-closed tickets whose dependencies are either empty or completely satisfied by tickets in status: closed.
  • Blocked Queue: All non-closed tickets where at least one dependency in deps is in status: open or status: in_progress.
  • Cycle Detection: Depth-First Search (DFS) traversal identifying circular references (\(A \to B \to A\)) across open tickets.

items.title: 4. CLI Interface & Exit Codes
items.text: Command Description tk init [path] Initializes .tickets/ tracking repository tk create <title> [options] Creates ticket, prints generated ID to stdout tk start <id> Sets status to in_progress tk close <id> Sets status to closed tk reopen <id> Sets status to open tk status <id> <status> Updates status directly (open, in_progress, closed) tk dep <id> <dep-id> Adds dependency relationship tk undep <id> <dep-id> Removes dependency relationship tk link <id> <link-id> Adds symmetric relational link between tickets tk unlink <id> <link-id> Removes symmetric relational link between tickets tk dep tree <id> Prints hierarchical ASCII dependency tree tk dep cycle Traverses graph and outputs detected cycles tk ready Lists unblocked, actionable tickets tk blocked Lists blocked tickets with unresolved blockers tk closed [--limit=N] Lists recently closed tickets tk ls / tk list [options] Lists tickets (default: hides closed, limit 10, with filters) tk edit <id> Opens ticket in $EDITOR tk query [jq-filter] Outputs tickets as JSON lines, with optional jq filter tk find <search-term> Case-insensitive text search across tickets tk show <id> Displays ticket metadata and full markdown body tk update <id> [options] Updates fields (title, desc, priority, tags, etc.) tk add-note <id> [text] Appends timestamped note tk agent-skill [--install] Displays or installs agent skill to ~/.agents/skills/tk/ tk version / --version Prints version, description, and license information tk help Displays available built-in commands and discovered plugins

items.title: 5. Plugin & Extension Protocol
items.text:
1. Any executable named tk-<command> or ticket-<command> in $PATH or located within plugins/<command>/ is automatically invoked when running tk <command>.
  2. When invoked, the core CLI exports:
  3. TICKETS_DIR: Absolute path to the resolved .tickets directory.
  4. TK_SCRIPT: Absolute path to the root tk executable.
  5. Plugins must conform to PLUGIN_SPEC.md:
  6. Directory isolation: plugins/<plugin-name>/ containing executable and <PLUGIN-NAME>-SPEC.md.
  7. Optionality: Except for tk-webui, all plugins are optional.
  8. Metadata discovery: # tk-plugin: <description> comment in header or --tk-describe flag for tk help discovery.
  9. Version contract: --version flag for standardized version reporting.

items.title: Agent Skill
items.text: ticket provides a native Agent Skill (agent-skill/tk/SKILL.md) designed to equip AI coding assistants with deep knowledge of tk task management and DAG dependency intelligence.

items.title: 🤖 What is the Agent Skill?
items.text: The agent skill instructs AI agents on: - Autonomous Execution: Following the 5-step lifecycle (tk ready -> tk start -> tk show -> tk add-note -> tk close). - Dependency Awareness: Managing parent-child tasks and blockers. - Review Audits: Logging clear timestamped notes.

items.title: ⚡ Installation
items.text:
You can install the agent skill locally or via npx directly from GitHub:

# Using installed tk CLI
tk agent-skill --install

# Or directly via npx without manual cloning
npx github:msampathkumar/ticket agent-skill --install

This installs the skill file to ~/.agents/skills/tk/SKILL.md, making it immediately available to your AI coding agents.

items.text:
graph TD

    B -->|Discovers Actions| C["1. tk ready (Discover)"]
    B -->|Discovers Actions| D["2. tk start <id> (Claim)"]
    B -->|Discovers Actions| E["3. tk show <id> (Inspect)"]
    B -->|Discovers Actions| F["4. tk add-note <id> (Audit)"]
    B -->|Discovers Actions| G["5. tk close <id> (Resolve)"]

items.title: LLM Context (llms.txt)
items.text:
Inspired by llmstxt.org and Model Context Protocol, ticket provides dedicated machine-readable documentation endpoints at root:

  • /llms.txt: Structured table of contents linking directly to all markdown documentation files and guides with summaries.
  • /llms-full.txt: Consolidated single-file documentation reference combining all specifications and guides into a single context-window-friendly payload.

items.title: How AI Agents Use llms.txt
items.text: When an AI coding assistant or agent visits a repository or documentation site supporting llms.txt: 1. It fetches /llms.txt to discover the exact structure and markdown URLs of all guides and specs. 2. It fetches specific markdown files or /llms-full.txt to instantly load complete technical context without web crawling or HTML scraping.

items.title: Agent Execution Loop
items.text:
When operating inside repositories tracked by ticket, autonomous AI coding agents follow a deterministic 5-step execution loop:

flowchart LR
    A["1. Query Actionable Work
`tk ready`"] --> B["2. Claim Ticket
`tk start <id>`"]
    B --> C["3. Inspect & Decompose
`tk show <id>`"]
    C --> D["4. Execute & Audit
`tk add-note <id> '...'`"]
    D --> E["5. Close & Unblock
`tk close <id>`"]

items.title: The 5-Step Loop
items.text:
1. Discover Actionable Tasks: Run tk ready to list unblocked tickets whose dependencies have all been satisfied.
  2. Claim the Task: Run tk start <id> to transition status to in_progress.
  3. Inspect Requirements & Subtasks: Run tk show <id> to inspect design notes, acceptance criteria, and child tickets. Decompose complex tasks using tk create "<title>" --parent <id> and tk dep <child> <dependency>.
  4. Implement, Verify & Record Notes: Execute code changes, run tests (make test), and append review audit notes via tk add-note <id> "...".
  5. Close the Ticket: Run tk close <id> to mark complete and automatically unblock downstream dependent tickets.

items.title: Command Reference
items.text: The tk CLI provides a complete suite of commands for task management and dependency intelligence.

items.title: Core CRUD & Lifecycle
items.text: Command Description Example tk init [path] Initialize .tickets repository tk init tk create [title] Create a new ticket (returns ID) tk create "Fix login bug" -p 0 -t bug tk show <id> Display full ticket details tk show tic-c83r tk update <id> Update title, description, priority, tags tk update tic-c83r -p 1 --tags urgent tk start <id> Transition ticket to in_progress tk start tic-c83r tk close <id> Transition ticket to closed tk close tic-c83r tk reopen <id> Transition ticket back to open tk reopen tic-c83r tk edit <id> Open ticket markdown file in $EDITOR tk edit tic-c83r

items.title: Dependency Intelligence
items.text: Command Description Example tk dep <id> <dep-id> Add dependency (id depends on dep-id) tk dep tic-2 tic-1 tk undep <id> <dep-id> Remove dependency relationship tk undep tic-2 tic-1 tk dep tree <id> Display recursive dependency tree tk dep tree tic-1 tk dep cycle Detect dependency cycles across open tickets tk dep cycle tk ready List unblocked actionable tasks tk ready tk blocked List tasks waiting on unresolved dependencies tk blocked

items.title: Querying & Listing
items.text: Command Description Example tk ls List tickets (hides closed, limit 10) tk ls -s open -p 1 tk query [jq] Output tickets as JSON, filterable with jq tk query '.[] | select(.priority==0)' tk find <term> Full-text search across all tickets tk find "authentication" tk add-note <id> [text] Append timestamped audit note tk add-note tic-1 "Tested successfully"

items.title: Dependency Intelligence
items.text: ticket (tk) treats task dependencies as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). This ensures tasks are completed in the correct logical sequence without circular deadlocks.

items.title: How Dependencies Work
items.text: When task B depends on task A: 1. B is considered blocked until A is closed. 2. tk ready will only show B after A transitions to closed. 3. Closing A automatically unblocks B.

items.title: Adding Dependencies
items.text:
# tic-backend-api must finish before tic-frontend-ui can start
tk dep tic-frontend-ui tic-backend-api

items.title: Cycle Detection
items.text:
To prevent circular deadlocks (e.g., A depends on B, B depends on A), tk includes native cycle detection: 

tk dep cycle

items.title: Viewing Dependency Trees
items.text:
Inspect recursive upstream and downstream relationships: 

tk dep tree tic-frontend-ui

items.title: Installation
items.text: ticket (tk) is designed with a zero-dependency POSIX Bash core and modular optional plugins. You can install only what you need.

items.title: ⚡ Quick Install
items.text:
Clone the repository and run the modular installer:

git clone https://github.com/msampathkumar/ticket.git
cd ticket

# Full Suite (CLI + Web UI + Agent Skill) — default
./install.sh --full

Binaries are installed to ~/.local/bin/ (tk, tk-webui, plus optional plugin binaries). Ensure ~/.local/bin is in your $PATH.

items.title: 🧩 Modular Installation Flags
items.text:
The installer supports composable flags so you can install precisely the components you require:

Flag Description Mandatory Dependencies --core Installs only the core tk POSIX Bash CLI Zero (Pure Bash) --webui Installs the interactive Kanban & DAG Web UI (tk-webui) Python 3.9+, FastAPI --skill Installs the AI agent skill (tk-agent-skill) None --github Installs the optional GitHub sync plugin (tk-github) Python / Bash --scion-taskforce Installs the autonomous SCION Task Force worker orchestrator (tk-scion-taskforce) Python 3.9+, scion CLI --full (Default) Installs Core CLI, Web UI, and Agent Skill Python 3.9+ (for Web UI) --all Installs everything, including optional plugins Python 3.9+, scion CLI

items.title: Examples
items.text:
# Install only the lightweight core CLI (no Python/Node required)
./install.sh --core

# Install Core CLI + GitHub sync plugin
./install.sh --core --github

# Install everything including optional plugins
./install.sh --all

items.title: Quick Start
items.text: Follow this 60-second quick start guide to initialize your first project, create tasks, manage dependencies, and launch the Web UI.

items.title: Step 1: Initialize a Project
items.text:
Navigate to your repository and initialize .tickets/: 

cd my-project
tk init
This creates a .tickets/ directory where all tasks are stored as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter.

items.title: Step 2: Create a Task
items.text:
Create your first task with priority and tags: 

tk create "Implement user authentication" \
  -d "Add JWT-based auth to FastAPI backend" \
  -p 1 \
  --tags backend,security
tk prints the generated task ID (e.g., tic-abc1).

items.title: Step 3: Check Actionable Work (tk ready)
items.text:
Run tk ready to list unblocked tasks whose dependencies are fully satisfied: 

tk ready

items.title: Step 4: Claim & Work on the Task
items.text:
Mark the task as in progress: 

tk start tic-abc1
Add review notes or progress logs: 
tk add-note tic-abc1 "Completed token generation logic and unit tests."

items.title: Step 5: Close the Task & Unblock Dependents
items.text:
When finished, close the task: 

tk close tic-abc1
This automatically updates the status and unblocks any downstream dependent tasks.

items.title: Step 6: Launch the Interactive Web UI
items.text:
Launch the 4-lane Kanban board and DAG Mind Map: 

tk webui
Open http://localhost:8475 in your browser.

items.title: Plugin Architecture
items.text: ticket features a lightweight, zero-overhead plugin architecture based on executable discovery.

items.title: How Plugins Work
items.text:
When you execute: 

tk <command> [args...]
The tk dispatcher looks for an executable named tk-<command> or ticket-<command> in your system $PATH. If found, execution is delegated directly to that binary or script.

To bypass plugins and run a built-in command directly, use tk super <command>.

items.title: Environment Context Passed to Plugins
items.text: When tk launches a plugin, it exports two environment variables: - TICKETS_DIR: Absolute path to active .tickets directory. - TK_SCRIPT: Absolute path to root tk executable ("$TK_SCRIPT" super ...).

items.title: Example Plugin (tk-stats)
items.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tk-plugin: Quick summary of open and closed ticket statistics
# tk-plugin-version: 1.0.0
set -euo pipefail

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--version" || "${1:-}" == "-v" ]]; then
    echo "tk-stats 1.0.0"
    exit 0
fi

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--tk-describe" ]]; then
    echo "tk-plugin: Quick summary of open and closed ticket statistics"
    exit 0
fi

TICKETS_DIR="${TICKETS_DIR:-.tickets}"
open=$("$TK_SCRIPT" super ready | wc -l || echo 0)
echo "🟢 Ready Tasks: $open"
Place in ~/.local/bin/tk-stats and run tk stats.

items.title: GitHub Sync
items.text: The optional GitHub plugin (tk-github) enables bi-directional synchronization between your local .tickets/ markdown files and GitHub issues and pull requests.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Import GitHub Issues: Pull GitHub issues directly into local markdown tickets with correct mapping of labels, assignees, and descriptions.
  • Push & Update: Push local ticket updates to GitHub or sync status changes when PRs are merged or closed.
  • Clean Unsyncing: Safely unlink and clean up external references without losing local history.

Install via: 

./install.sh --github

items.title: SCION Task Force
items.text: The SCION Task Force (tk-scion-taskforce) is an optional standalone orchestrator plugin that manages autonomous coding workers mapped 1:1 to tickets.

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
1. Watchdog Daemon: A single global daemon (~/.local/state/tk/scion-taskforce.json) watches tk ready tickets tagged with taskforce.
  2. Worker Spawning: Automatically spawns a SCION coding worker mapped to the ticket ID.
  3. Review Pause: Automatically pauses workers on waiting-for-review, relays feedback, and emits OpenTelemetry to local rotating logs (30-day retention).

Install via: 

./install.sh --scion-taskforce

items.title: Daemon Management
items.text: You can run the Web UI as a persistent background daemon so it is always ready when you need it.

items.title: Daemon Commands
items.text:
# Start background daemon on http://127.0.0.1:8475
tk webui server start [optional-project-path]

# Inspect daemon PID, URL, and log file path
tk webui server status

# Stop background daemon
tk webui server stop

# Restart daemon
tk webui server restart

Logs are automatically rotated and stored locally for debugging.

items.title: Overview & Kanban
items.text: The Web UI (tk-webui) is an optional, high-performance visual dashboard running on port 8475 (ASCII for T = 84, K = 75).

items.title: 🖥️ Visual Showcase
items.text: 4-Lane Kanban Board Interactive Dependency Graph Create & Edit Ticket Table & Filter View

items.title: Key UI Features
items.text:
• 4-Lane Kanban Board: Fluid drag-and-drop between Ready, In Progress, Blocked, and Closed lanes.
  • Interactive Mind Map & DAG Graph: Visualize task dependencies, filter by status, toggle top-down or left-to-right layouts, and expand/collapse subtrees.
  • Multi-View Switcher: Instantly toggle between Kanban, Table View, Dependency Tree Graph, and Timeline/Gantt View.
  • In-Place Task Editing: Edit titles, descriptions, tags, priorities, assignees, design notes, and acceptance criteria in real time.
  • PR-Style Review Comments: Chronological audit trail for review notes and comments (Cmd+Enter to submit).

items.title: Launching the Web UI
items.text:
# Start foreground server
tk webui

# Or start as a background daemon
tk webui server start
Access the dashboard at http://localhost:8475.

items.title: Solo CLI Workflow
items.text: The Solo CLI Workflow is designed for software engineers, solo founders, and terminal power users who want rapid, offline task tracking without leaving their shell.

items.title: 🧭 Visual Lifecycle
items.text:
flowchart LR
    A["tk init<br/>Initialize repo"] --> B["tk create<br/>Capture idea"]
    B --> C["tk ready<br/>Query work"]
    C --> D["tk start<br/>Begin coding"]
    D --> E["tk add-note<br/>Document"]
    E --> F["tk close<br/>Mark complete"]

    style A fill:#6366f1,stroke:#4f46e5,color:#fff
    style B fill:#3b82f6,stroke:#2563eb,color:#fff
    style C fill:#10b981,stroke:#059669,color:#fff

    style F fill:#ec4899,stroke:#db2777,color:#fff

items.title: 1. Initialize Once
items.text:
Inside your Git project root: 

tk init
This creates .tickets/. All task metadata is versioned directly with your code.

items.title: 2. Rapid Task Creation
items.text:
Create tickets on the fly without breaking your flow: 

tk create "Add SQLite caching layer" -p 1 -t feature --tags database,performance

items.title: 3. Check Ready Tasks
items.text:
Instead of scanning endless lists, let tk compute what is actionable right now: 

tk ready

items.title: 4. Work & Add Notes
items.text:
Mark your ticket in progress and record design thoughts: 

tk start tic-10a
tk add-note tic-10a "Evaluated in-memory cache vs WAL mode; choosing WAL mode."

items.title: 5. Close and Unblock
items.text:
When complete, close the task: 

tk close tic-10a
Any dependent tasks are automatically unblocked and immediately appear in tk ready.

items.title: SCION Task Force Workflow
items.text: The SCION Task Force Workflow empowers teams to delegate actionable engineering tasks directly to autonomous coding agents while maintaining total oversight through human-in-the-loop review checkpoints.

items.title: 🧭 Visual Lifecycle
items.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Developer as Human Developer
    participant TK as ticket (.tickets/)
    participant Daemon as SCION Daemon
    participant Worker as Autonomous AI Worker

    Developer->>TK: Creates ticket & tags 'taskforce'
    Daemon->>TK: Polls `tk ready` with tag:taskforce
    Daemon->>Worker: Spawns 1:1 worker container
    Worker->>TK: Runs `tk start <id>`
    Worker->>Worker: Writes code & executes tests
    Worker->>TK: Runs `tk add-note` & sets tag `waiting-for-review`
    Worker->>Daemon: Pauses execution
    Developer->>TK: Reviews notes & diffs in Web UI
    Developer->>TK: Approves & closes ticket (`tk close <id>`)
    Daemon->>Worker: Terminates worker cleanly

items.title: 1. Tag Work for Autonomous Execution
items.text:
Human engineers explicitly choose which tickets to delegate by adding the taskforce tag: 

tk create "Add input sanitization to auth endpoints" \
  -p 1 \
  --tags backend,taskforce \
  --acceptance "Run make test and ensure all pass"

items.title: 2. Daemon Worker Spawning
items.text:
The global SCION daemon notices the ready ticket and provisions an isolated coding worker: 

tk scion-taskforce status

items.title: 3. Review Checkpoint
items.text: When the worker finishes writing code and passing local tests: 1. It records verification notes via tk add-note <id> "...". 2. It tags the ticket with waiting-for-review. 3. The worker pauses execution.

items.title: 4. Human Verification & Closure
items.text:
The developer opens the Web UI (http://localhost:8475), reviews the audit trail and code diff, and closes the ticket: 

tk close tic-auth1
Closing the ticket automatically unblocks any downstream tasks in the DAG!

items.title: 1. Launch the Background Daemon
items.text:
Keep your web dashboard running persistently without tying up your active shell: 

tk webui server start
Check status or logs at any time: 
tk webui server status

items.title: 2. Visualize Sprint & Mind Map
items.text: Open http://localhost:8475 in your browser: - Switch to Mind Map View to see dependencies, parent-child task links, and critical paths. - Switch to Kanban Board to drag tasks seamlessly between Ready, In Progress, Blocked, and Closed lanes.

items.title: 3. Collaborative Review
items.text:
• Open any task drawer to review design notes and acceptance criteria.
  • Append chronological audit notes with Cmd+Enter.
